fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Corrected to the official completed 2026 Gran Fondo: 97 km / 755 m, with elevations only from roughly 100-326 m and a sold-out 4,000-rider international weekend. Distance is 3, altitude 1, field depth 5, and climate risk 2 for the profile's mild 15-25 C May conditions; score recalculates to 64.

course_description.character: The completed 2026 Gran Fondo covered 97 km around the north side of Qiandao Lake with 755 m of climbing. Four categorized climbs created repeated punchy efforts, but none was long or especially steep. The course otherwise favored fast group riding on well-paved lakeside and countryside roads, with a feed zone after 60 km. Saturday's separate time trial used a flat 21 km out-and-back course.
course_description.signature_challenge: Repeated short climbs and fast group positioning on the 97 km Qiandao Lake loop

logistics.transport: Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport (HGH) is the main gateway. The time trial and Gran Fondo use separate venues, so confirm the next edition's transfer and check-in details before booking.

history.origin_story: Founded 2025 as China's first UCI Gran Fondo World Series event and first international A-class cycling in Hangzhou post-2023 Asian Games. 2025 debut (Sep 6-7) drew 1,500+ riders from 30 countries as final qualifier for UCI World Championships. 2026 edition May 23-24 on 2022 Asian Games course.

biased_opinion.summary: Hangzhou pairs a huge international UCI qualifier field with a fast, scenic Qiandao Lake course. The completed 2026 Gran Fondo covered 97 km with 755 m of climbing and rewarded repeated short efforts plus efficient pack riding more than high-mountain durability.

final_verdict.one_liner: A sold-out, 4,000-rider UCI qualifier on a fast 97 km / 755 m loop around Qiandao Lake.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if you want a large international age-group qualifier with fast packs and repeated short climbs. Wait for official next-edition facts before booking travel; no 2027 date or course is published yet.
